newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gasoline hurt by crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gasoline hurt by crude.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Thursday with a late sharp drop in crude prices weighing on gasoline.
Gasoline was lower tracking a sharp drop in futures but activity was thinned by Friday's All Saints' holiday.
"In Italy the mogas market is fairly well balanced," and more subject to moves in Brent, said one trader.

She said an Italian refinery was believed to be short a cargo of unleaded premium for early Nov delivery into southern depots. Another refinery was expected to have availability of winter spec premium in the third decade of November.
Naphtha also slipped after crude turned lower and end user demand was seen dormant for the time being.
Gas oil trade remained very thin, with 0.2 heating firmer by up to $2 on bullish fundamentals.

"It's up a couple of dollars. Most of the cargoes are sold. All the Russians are gone. Most of the Italian is sold," one trader said. A cargo was traded into Sete for Nov 20-25 dates with traders assessing the deal at high cif quotes +$1.25.
A cargo of heating oil (-5/-15) was sold cif high +$4 basis Koper, including a $1 premium for Koper and $1.50 for the French cold properties, traders said.
The low sulphur market remained dormant, with premiums probably headed lower on lack of demand.
High sulphur fuel oil was flat for most of the day although a sharp late sell-off in the futures market dampened sentiment.

At least two players were heard seeking bunker quality material. A trader bought a Russian M-100 cargo in northwest Europe and dealers thought this likely to move to cover a requirement in the Canaries.
Low sulphur markets were quiet after the sale of a trader's prompt cargo on Wednesday to an Italian utility.
